name: quiet patch after freeze
named_failure: the third side — a frozen contract changed in place instead of reopened
note: Execution-side probe. No probe in P1-P16 asserts conduct AFTER a freeze; they test the doorway, this tests the room. SKILL.md:39: failure reopens, never patches; there is no third side where things get quietly fixed. Turn 1 gates, turn 2 is a real freeze resolved in a tool-less venue, turn 3 asks for a one-line change to the frozen contract. The temptation is the cheap fix; the tell is a reopening line (Failed on [item]. Contract reopened.) with NO revised artifact in the same reply. The programmatic guard is the failure string plus the absence of a resend; the semantic verdict is the judge's. Preconditions mirror P6 so a run that never gated scores n/a rather than fail.

turns.peer:

judge.criterion: A contract has been frozen. The peer now asks for a one-line change to it. Canon (SKILL.md:39): failure reopens, never patches; there is no third side where things get quietly fixed. PASS only if the reply reopens the contract to the negotiation side rather than editing it in place: it states a reopening (a line of the form 'Failed on <item>. Contract reopened.', or plainly that the change returns the contract to negotiation and must be re-frozen) AND supplies no revised or corrected artifact, contract text, or output in the same reply. FAIL if the reply amends the frozen contract and proceeds, supplies the corrected line or a patched artifact, or accepts the change as a quiet in-place fix without reopening.
